rules.title: Pre-participation screening and conservative mode
rules.statement: Eight-question screen at onboarding (ACSM 2015 logic, PAR-Q+ domains, original wording). Symptoms, or known disease while inactive, recommend medical clearance and set conservative mode until the user confirms clearance.
rules.uncertainty: Screen wording is original and untested; licence check needed before using PAR-Q+ text verbatim.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Red-flag symptoms trigger SAFETY STOP
rules.statement: Chest pain/pressure, fainting or near-fainting, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, palpitations, sudden severe pain, or stroke-like signs end the session immediately with calm guidance; emergency number shown; resume only after user confirms resolution or medical review; first session back LIGHT.
rules.uncertainty: Symptom list is conservative by design.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: In-session pain protocol
rules.statement: Pain is a separate gate from readiness. Joint/tendon pain <=3/10 not worsening: continue with load -10-20% or shorter range. 4-6/10 or worsening: stop the exercise, offer substitutes with joint stress <=1 for that joint, region to conservative mode. >=7/10 or sharp, swelling, instability, locking, numbness/tingling, or after a fall: stop loading the region, end session if whole-body movement affected, suggest a professional.
rules.uncertainty: Thresholds are expert practice; rehab data (supervised) allow up to 5/10.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Persistent pain and region conservative mode
rules.statement: Same region painful in >=2 sessions or >7 days: suggest a physiotherapist/doctor; region stays conservative (joint stress <=1, RIR >=3, no failure, no jumping) until 2 consecutive pain-free sessions, then +1 stress level per week.
rules.uncertainty: No direct evidence for the exact return sequence.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Hard workload caps
rules.statement: The engine never prescribes beyond these caps; neither the AI coach nor repeated taps can bypass them.
rules.uncertainty: Cap values are expert practice set below volumes tolerated in studies because conditioning is concurrent.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: peer-reviewed Pelland 2026 replaces the 2024 preprint (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: User additions: warn, confirm, absolute ceiling
rules.statement: User may deviate. Additions beyond a cap require explicit per-addition confirmation and are logged and counted. Absolute ceiling stops accidental runaway. Additions to a painful region are blocked.
rules.uncertainty: Product rule.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Illness gate
rules.statement: Fever, chills, body aches, chest symptoms, vomiting or diarrhoea lock the day to RECOVERY (rest). Return per REG-005.
rules.uncertainty: Expert practice ('neck check' style).
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Final pre-render safety validator
rules.statement: Every generated or modified session is checked: per-muscle and per-session sets, weekly SSU and planned load, HIIT count and spacing, pattern balance, pain-region exclusions, contraindications, tier compliance, screening mode, failure policy. Auto-correct and log; fallback to LIGHT; never crash; never display unvalidated.
rules.uncertainty: Engineering requirement.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: AI coach boundary
rules.statement: Coach explains engine decisions from the Decision Log and rule IDs; no diagnosis, medication/supplement or extreme-diet advice; can only request engine actions which the engine validates; never writes sets, reps or loads; output safety-filtered; embedded instructions treated as data; offline fallback to Tier 1.
rules.uncertainty: Engineering requirement.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Coaching voice
rules.statement: Calm, competent, honest, brief, non-judgemental. No body-shaming, guilt, punishment exercise, extreme motivation or 'no pain, no gain'.
rules.uncertainty: Product rule.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: WHO floor accounting
rules.statement: Equivalent minutes = Z1 (including STEP-002 brisk walks) + 2 × (Z2 + Z3 work); target ≥150/week; muscle-strengthening ≥2 days.
rules.change_reason: MINOR: Defines 'optional logged walking' so steps are never counted twice. (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Training days per week
rules.statement: Train 2-6 days/week with at least one full rest day; default 3 when unknown (ASSUMPTION).
rules.uncertainty: Upper bound is expert practice.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: ACSM 2026 full text checked (first author, volume, pages, DOI corrected); no parameter changes

rules.title: Per-muscle exposures
rules.statement: Each major muscle gets >=2 exposures/week; an exposure is >=2 fractional hard sets in one session.
rules.uncertainty: With volume equated frequency matters little for hypertrophy; it is a volume-distribution tool.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: peer-reviewed Pelland 2026 replaces the 2024 preprint (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Resistance training days
rules.statement: Resistance training on >=2 days every week.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: ACSM 2026 full text checked (first author, volume, pages, DOI corrected); no parameter changes

rules.title: Main-pattern frequency in strength blocks
rules.statement: Squat, hinge, horizontal push and horizontal pull loaded 2-3 x/week in strength blocks.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: peer-reviewed Pelland 2026 replaces the 2024 preprint (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Aerobic exposure distribution
rules.statement: Aerobic work appears on >=3 days/week when training >=3 days; short post-strength blocks count.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Hard set definition
rules.statement: A hard set is a working set ending at RIR <=4 (RPE >=6). Warm-up sets and RIR >=5 count zero.
rules.uncertainty: Exact proximity threshold for a 'stimulating' set is uncertain.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Fractional set counting
rules.statement: 1.0 set to each primary muscle, 0.5 to each secondary, 0 to stabilisers.
rules.uncertainty: Peer-reviewed meta-regression (Pelland 2026): fractional set counting fitted best. Participants' mean age was about 25, so transfer to adults 30+ is assumed.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: peer-reviewed Pelland 2026 replaces the 2024 preprint (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Volume landmarks (fractional sets/muscle/week)
rules.statement: Blocks start at 'start'; usual working range; the engine never plans above 'cap'. Landmark names are coaching vocabulary.
rules.uncertainty: Individual response varies widely; values for small muscles may differ.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: peer-reviewed Pelland 2026 replaces the 2024 preprint (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Fatigue-driven volume reduction
rules.statement: If >=2 fatigue signals (DEL-001) persist across >=2 sessions, accessory sets drop 30% until they clear.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Per-session per-muscle cap
rules.statement: Direct hard sets per muscle per session <= cap by level.
rules.uncertainty: Per-session dose ceiling poorly studied.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: peer-reviewed Pelland 2026 replaces the 2024 preprint (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Weekly volume progression within a block
rules.statement: Each week a muscle may gain sets only if its exercises held or improved and no fatigue signal is active.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Systemic stress units (planning)
rules.statement: SSU = sum over sets C_ex x E_RIR + sum over conditioning t_min x Z_zone x J_modality. Weekly SSU <= level ceiling and (after 4 weeks) <= 1.15 x 3-week mean. Personal factor k = median(sRPE load / SSU) after 4 weeks.
rules.uncertainty: Novel model; coefficients are judgement and must be validated in Phase 4 simulations.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Working sets per session cap
rules.statement: Working sets per session (including core) <= cap.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: RPE-RIR mapping validity
rules.statement: RIR = 10 - RPE used only from RPE 6 to 10 on working sets.
rules.uncertainty: RIR error ~1 rep; larger far from failure and in novices.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: RIR targets
rules.statement: Targets by level and exercise class; week 1 of a block +1 RIR, last loading week -1 (not below floor).
rules.change_reason: PATCH: ACSM 2026 full text checked (first author, volume, pages, DOI corrected); no parameter changes

rules.title: Failure policy
rules.statement: RIR 0 only on the last set of FailureSafe exercises (machine, cable, isolation dumbbell, safe bodyweight), <=2 exercises/session, FULL tier, not in deload, not beginners' first 8 weeks, never on failure-unsafe lifts.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: evidence added (single set to failure vs 2 RIR; Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Estimated 1RM (Epley, RIR-adjusted)
rules.statement: e1RM = load x (1 + (reps + RIR)/30); update only from sets with reps+RIR <= 12 and RIR <= 3; session value = best valid set; smoothed E <- E + 0.4 (S - E); single update capped at +5%.
rules.uncertainty: Formula accuracy falls above ~10 reps and varies by lift.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Load selection from e1RM
rules.statement: load = e1RM / (1 + (target reps + target RIR)/30), then rounded per PROG-003; without e1RM use CAL-001.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Teaching effort to beginners
rules.statement: First 4 weeks: rep targets plus 'how many more could you have done? 0/1/2/3/4+'; RPE language introduced gradually.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: In-session autoregulation
rules.statement: After the first working set: RPE < target-1 with reps hit -> +1 increment (<=5%); RPE > target+1 or reps below range -> -5%; net change <= +/-10% per exercise per session.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Strength range
rules.statement: 3-6 reps at ~80-88% 1RM; 1-3 only for advanced at RPE <=8.
rules.uncertainty: Exact range is practice.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: ACSM 2026 full text checked (first author, volume, pages, DOI corrected); no parameter changes

rules.title: Hypertrophy range
rules.statement: Compounds 6-12, isolation 8-20 near target RIR.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Muscular endurance range
rules.statement: 15-30 reps or 30-60 s at <60% 1RM.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Power
rules.statement: 3-5 reps at 30-70% 1RM with maximal intent; reps x sets < 24; stop when speed visibly drops.
rules.uncertainty: No velocity device; subjective speed-drop rule.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: ACSM 2026 full text checked (first author, volume, pages, DOI corrected); no parameter changes

rules.title: Core dosing
rules.statement: Holds 10-45 s or 6-12 controlled reps per side.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Conditioning units
rules.statement: Minutes, metres, watts, calories or reps by modality.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Heavy compounds
rules.statement: >=80% or <=6 reps: 120-300 s, default 180 s.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Moderate compounds
rules.statement: 6-12 reps: 90-150 s, default 120 s.
rules.uncertainty: ACSM 2026: inter-set rest did not consistently change outcomes, so defaults are practical and may be compressed under time pressure.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: evidence added (ACSM 2026 on rest intervals); no parameter changes

rules.title: Isolation / accessories
rules.statement: 60-90 s, default 75 s.
rules.uncertainty: ACSM 2026: inter-set rest did not consistently change outcomes, so defaults are practical and may be compressed under time pressure.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: evidence added (ACSM 2026 on rest intervals); no parameter changes

rules.title: Non-competing supersets
rules.statement: 45-75 s between paired exercises, default 60 s.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Circuits
rules.statement: 15-45 s transitions, default 30 s.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Core
rules.statement: 30-60 s, default 45 s.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Autoregulated rest and compression
rules.statement: User may start next set anywhere in range; timer alerts at default; under time pressure rests shrink toward minimum, accessories first, heavy compounds last and never below minimum.
rules.uncertainty: ACSM 2026: inter-set rest did not consistently change outcomes, so defaults are practical and may be compressed under time pressure.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: evidence added (ACSM 2026 on rest intervals); no parameter changes

rules.title: Session sequence
rules.statement: Warm-up -> power/skill -> primary compound -> secondary compound -> accessories -> core -> conditioning -> cool-down.
rules.change_reason: PATCH: ACSM 2026 full text checked (first author, volume, pages, DOI corrected); no parameter changes

rules.title: Order exceptions
rules.statement: Conditioning-priority day: conditioning moves to step 3 and lower-body strength volume -30%. Weak point may precede secondary compounds. Restricted-joint mobility moves into warm-up.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Superset eligibility
rules.statement: Only non-competing pairs at one station or within a few steps; never heavy main lifts at RIR <=2; never across two stations in a crowded gym.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Strength first in shared sessions
rules.statement: Resistance before conditioning except conditioning-priority days.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Same-day separation
rules.statement: Two hard sessions on one day separated by >=6 h, else merged strength-first.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: HIIT vs heavy legs
rules.statement: No HIIT in ~24 h before heavy lower-body or power session; same day HIIT after strength.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Low-impact modality preference
rules.statement: Low-impact, concentric-dominant modalities first; impact work <=1/week and not the day before heavy legs. A short bone-loading block from the osteoporosis condition entry (≤5 min, low-level landings such as heel drops or small hops, ≥50 landings) is not an impact session under this rule.
rules.change_reason: MINOR: SAF-010 osteoporosis entry: the UK consensus advises moderate impact most days; the weekly impact-session cap was written for jumping conditioning work. (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Power protection
rules.statement: Power work at session start; never after HIIT the same day.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Aerobic dose in strength blocks
rules.statement: Mostly Z1 and ≤150 prescribed gym minutes/week in strength-emphasis blocks. For the fat-loss goal, brisk walks (STEP-002) are outside this cap.
rules.change_reason: MINOR: Fat-loss targets of 200–300 min/week (FL-002) would otherwise clash with the cap; walking adds little interference with strength gains (Research Update 1.1). (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Aerobic intensity zones
rules.statement: Talk test + CR10, optional %HRR: Z1 easy (full sentences, CR10 3-4, 40-59% HRR, moderate), Z2 tempo (talk not comfortable, CR10 5-6, 60-79%, vigorous), Z3 intervals (few words, CR10 7-9, >=80%, vigorous), Z4 sprint (CR10 10).
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Weekly intensity distribution
rules.statement: About 75-80% of aerobic minutes in Z1; remainder Z2/Z3 incl. HIIT.
rules.uncertainty: Distribution evidence comes from endurance athletes.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Aerobic progression
rules.statement: Duration first (+2-5 min/session, <=+15%/week) to ~30-40 min Z1; then Z2 tempo; then intervals.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Weekly HIIT ceiling
rules.statement: <=2/week; 3rd only for intermediate/advanced, FULL day, no fatigue signal or workload flag, conditioning block. >=6 min Z3 work or a circuit at CR10 >=7 for >=8 min counts as HIIT.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: HIIT protocol menu
rules.statement: Protocol chosen by block and purpose, not popularity.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: HIIT prerequisites
rules.statement: Screen clear or cleared, calibration done, >=3 weeks Z1 base; first HIIT short 1:2 at CR10 7-8.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: HIIT spacing
rules.statement: >=48 h preferred, 24 h minimum between HIIT sessions, plus CON-003.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Per-session HIIT work caps
rules.statement: Long <=20 min work, short <=10 min, sprint <=2.5 min; <=35 min conditioning after strength.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Excluded modalities
rules.statement: Cardio machines are a per-person choice: each user keeps a list of modalities they don't use (set at onboarding, editable). Treadmill running is off by default for the fat-loss goal (impact) and can be turned on; treadmill walking (including incline walking), stationary and air bikes and stair machines are available when the gym has them and the user hasn't excluded them. The Product Owner's own profile keeps treadmill running, stationary bikes and stair machines excluded (Part 0).
rules.uncertainty: User constraint.
rules.change_reason: MAJOR: Research Update 1.1 decision 2 (approved 2026-10-09 with the recommended option): a market-ready weight-loss app for 30+ needs the common joint-friendly machines; the exclusions came from the Product Owner's personal equipment list. (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Modality matrix and selection score
rules.statement: Score = 0.35 stimulus fit + 0.25 (1-interference/5) x leg priority + 0.20 (1-impact/5) x joint sensitivity + 0.10 variety + 0.10 preference.
rules.uncertainty: Ratings are expert judgement. Matrix rows for the five machines made selectable by MOD-001 2.0.0 are Expert Practice values, in the same 0–5 style as the existing rows; running scores impact 4, so it counts toward CON-004.
rules.change_reason: MINOR: Direct consequence of decision 2 (MOD-001 2.0.0): the newly selectable machines need scores to be ranked; added during implementation (D-066). (Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09)

rules.title: Weekly pattern coverage
rules.statement: >=3 days: patterns 1-7 each >=1x, squat/hinge/h-push/h-pull >=2x, carry >=1x, anti-ext/anti-rot/anti-lat >=1x, rotation >=1x per 2 weeks. 2 days: 1-7 and 10-12 weekly; carry and rotation alternate weeks.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Pull:push ratio
rules.statement: Weekly pulling sets / pushing sets between 1.0 and 1.5.
rules.change_reason: Initial version; approved at Phase 1 sign-off

rules.title: Knee:hip ratio

rules.title: Default goal: lose fat, keep muscle
rules.statement: For adults 30+ the default goal is 'Lose fat, keep muscle'; every other goal stays selectable. Aerobic minutes are the main fat-loss lever and strength training protects muscle; HIIT counts as aerobic minutes but is never presented as a fat-loss accelerator. The app shows a realistic expectation: without changing what you eat, about 2–3 kg and a 2–5 cm smaller waist over a few months at 150–300 min/week, and it never promises faster loss. No food or calorie features. Anyone can turn weight features off (no weight or waist tracking, expectations or rate check-in; the default goal becomes general fitness). With pregnancy, or cancer in active treatment, the fat-loss goal is not offered and weight features are off; after giving birth it is not the default and can be chosen from 12 weeks.
rules.uncertainty: Default goal and the age-30 threshold are product decisions (D-060). Weight and body-fat effects are GRADE moderate, waist high (Jayedi 2024); effects are trial totals over 8+ weeks, not weekly rates; no RCT shows exercise prevents regain. The weight-features opt-out protects people for whom weight focus is unhelpful without asking about eating disorders (Expert Practice).
rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1) — Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09

rules.title: Weekly activity target
rules.statement: Weekly target in equivalent minutes (PH-001 accounting: Z1 + 2 × Z2/Z3 work, brisk walks per STEP-002): 200–300 for ages 30–59, 180–250 for 60–64, 150–250 for 65+, never below 150. The target is approached from last week's minutes at ≤ +15%/week (AER-003), ≤ +12%/week at 65+ (AGE-001 × 0.8); steady Z1 work, mostly walking, is the base.
rules.uncertainty: Linear benefit to 300 min/week is from trials of 8+ weeks; the lower ceilings from 60 are Expert Practice (recovery and time), not evidence that older adults need less.
rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1) — Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09

rules.title: Training mix by age band
rules.statement: The weekly mix for the fat-loss goal changes with age: strength stays at 3 days by default (2 minimum) in every band; steady Z1 cardio stays at 150–200 min; tempo (Z2) and intervals shrink with age and become low-impact only from 50; a power-emphasis slot (light load lifted fast, low impact) is added from 50; balance work starts at 50 and becomes ≥3 multicomponent days at 65+. Interval sessions need a base of regular training first, longer with age.

age_30_39.impact_needs: BMI < 30 and no lower-limb pain; ≤1 impact session/week (CON-004)

rules.title: Fat-loss year
rules.statement: For the fat-loss goal the 12-month sequence is Calibrate(2) → Foundation → Build → Conditioning → Strength → Build II → Conditioning II → Athletic (low-impact power and conditioning) → Consolidation → Review(+2 flex). Every block keeps the FL-003 strength days and aerobic minutes; conditioning blocks shift gym time toward aerobic work without dropping below 2 strength days.

rules.title: Progress measures without food tracking
rules.statement: Waist and strength are the main progress measures; weight is secondary. Waist (optional): every 2–4 weeks, midway between the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone, standing, after a normal breath out, three readings averaged; South Asian reference lines (≥90 cm men, ≥80 cm women) shown as information only. Weight (optional): daily or weekly under the same conditions; the app shows a 7-day mean and judges only 4-week trends. If the 7-day mean falls more than 1 kg/week for 3 weeks in a row, a neutral check-in suggests checking with a doctor if the user isn't trying to diet or feels unwell. No food advice.

parameters.waist_site: midpoint lowest rib – top of iliac crest (WHO STEPS)

rules.uncertainty: Daily vs weekly weighing is equivalent (Moderate); averaging, the rate flag and the measuring site are Expert Practice. The Indian consensus measures just above the hip bone, not at the WHO midpoint; readings differ between sites.

rules.title: Daily step target
rules.statement: Daily step target by age band — 9,000 (30–49), 8,000 (50–59), 7,500 (60–64), 7,000 (65+) — reached gradually: baseline = median of the first 7 valid days (≥500 steps recorded); each week the target rises by p × last week's mean (p = 0.15 under 50, 0.10 from 50), rounded to 50 steps, between 250 and a cap (1,000 under 50, 750 at 50–59, 500 at 60–64, 400 at 65+), only if the target was met on ≥5 of 7 days; held at 3–4 days; lowered by one step after 2 weeks with ≤2 days met; no rise in a deload week or with a lower-limb pain flag; never above the band target.
rules.uncertainty: Targets come from observational mortality plateaus (8,000–10,000 under 60, 6,000–8,000 from 60) measured with research devices, not phones. The progression rate is Expert Practice; adaptive goals have Limited Evidence. Steps alone barely change weight (~0.05 kg/week).
rules.change_reason: CR-005 / D-062: phone step counter (Research Update 1.1) — Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09

rules.title: Brisk walks count as easy cardio
rules.statement: Only brisk-walk bouts — at least 10 minutes in a row at 100 steps/min or more, from the phone's step counter or logged by the user — count as Z1 minutes for PH-001, FL-002 and the AER-003 growth limit. All other steps count only toward the step target, so walking is never counted twice.
rules.uncertainty: Cadence threshold Moderate (Tudor-Locke 2011); the 10-minute bout rule is Expert Practice. Whether the phone sensor gives per-minute cadence offline is an engineering check for Part 3.
rules.change_reason: CR-005 / D-062 (Research Update 1.1) — Research Update 1.1, approved by the Product Owner on 2026-10-09

rules.title: Health-condition profiles
rules.statement: Users may select health conditions from a versioned table (health_conditions v1.0). Each entry sets conservative limits on general fitness training: doctor's OK advice, highest zone, intervals, minimum reps in reserve, no training to failure, impact, exercise tags to avoid, joint limits, extra warm-up and cool-down, positions, prompts and condition-specific stop signs. With several conditions each control takes its most restrictive value. Control status is self-reported (not sure = not under control); the app never reads or thresholds clinical values (blood pressure, glucose, ketones). A doctor's OK is the user's statement of scope (light–moderate, vigorous, intervals) and unlocks only that scope. Prompts never name a medicine, dose, value target or diagnosis, and never claim to treat a condition. A clinician and a regulatory adviser review the table before any public release.
rules.uncertainty: Benefit of exercise is High Evidence for type 2 diabetes, knee/hip osteoarthritis, high blood pressure and pregnancy; nearly every numeric cap is an Expert Practice translation of guideline intensity into app controls. Stroke, COPD and cancer entries rest on less-verified sources. Not a medical device feature: no diagnosis, no clinical values, no treatment claims (D-058).

rules.title: Starting from your own numbers
rules.statement: A user may enter, per exercise, a recent set (weight × reps and reps in reserve) or a best lift (counted as 0 reps in reserve). An estimated 1RM comes from INT-004 only when the entry is valid (reps + RIR ≤ 12, RIR ≤ 3); the first working load is the INT-005 load from 90% of that estimate (CAL-001 known-weights start). If the user last did the exercise 14–27 days ago the estimate is reduced 10%, 28–55 days 20%, and from 56 days the entry is used only as a ceiling for a normal CAL-001 ramp (age 60+ or a flagged screen moves one band longer, as REG-004). The first session confirms it with the CAL-001 rules.
rules.uncertainty: e1RM formula accuracy is Moderate (INT-004); the 90% start and the age reductions follow existing CAL-001/REG-004 values rather than direct evidence for self-reported numbers, which may be optimistic.

rules.title: Planning prompt
rules.statement: Optional and under 30 seconds: when the week is planned (or once at onboarding, editable), each training day gets a 'when' (day and time) and an optional 'after what' cue (e.g. after dropping the kids), and the user picks one if-then backup from a short list — e.g. 'If I'm short on time → the express session (ADH-004)'; 'If I miss the planned day → the next free day (REG-002)'. Same weekdays are suggested by default. Never nags; stored on the phone only.
rules.uncertainty: Planning helps physical activity in general (Moderate), but delivered online only the effect was not significant (Peng 2022: SMD 0.14, CI −0.02 to 0.31); low cost and no plausible harm.

rules.title: Calm mobility session
rules.statement: An optional 15–30-minute calm mobility session with original content: 2–3 min easy movement, slow flowing mobility for hips, upper back, shoulders and ankles, standing balance holds, holds of 30–60 s, and 3–5 min of easy slow breathing to finish (no breath holds, no special ratios). Offered — never imposed — on rest days as an alternative to MOB-005, on LIGHT and RECOVERY days (RDY-004), and when the check-in stress item is 1–2 (RDY-001). It does not count as Z1 minutes (PH-001, FL-002) or as a strength day; its balance holds count toward FL-003 balance minutes. All SAF-010 tags, joint limits and the SAF-003 pain protocol apply; no heated rooms. Wording says 'for mobility, balance and winding down' and never claims treatment, detox, weight loss or faster recovery.
rules.uncertainty: Benefits (flexibility, balance, sleep quality, perceived stress) are moderate vs inactivity and small vs other exercise; trials are small and often unblinded. Format, triggers and dose are Expert Practice. Yoga is light activity (~2.5 METs), has no effect on weight, and stretching does not speed recovery — hence the wording limits.

rules.title: Training away from the gym today
rules.statement: One tap sets today's equipment to the user's saved home kit (bodyweight only by default); the generator then substitutes as usual (SUB-001/002). Strength uses the BW-001 ladders at the plan's RIR. Conditioning defaults to no-jump bodyweight circuits; jumping only under the FL-003 / CON-004 conditions; beginners use 1:2 work:rest (HIIT-002); a circuit at CR10 ≥7 for ≥8 min counts as HIIT (HIIT-001). The warm-up floor applies even to short sessions (WU-003); 20–30-minute express versions are offered (ADH-004). If the home day cannot cover a movement pattern, the weekly check reports the shortfall (PAT-001).
rules.uncertainty: Home training improves fitness and strength (Moderate; home HIIT ≈ continuous training; older adults gain strength, power and balance). The preset itself is a Product Rule and its format Expert Practice. Jump-based home intervals were tested in young, lean adults, and plyometric safety data come from supervised programmes.
